hero.description: In a realm where light travels for billions of years to reach our eyes, every star tells a story from the distant past.

galaxies.label: Approximate number of galaxies in the universe

structure.title: The Structure of the Universe
structure.description: Our universe consists of structures ranging from incredibly small atoms to vast galaxy superclusters. The laws of physics operate in remarkable harmony across all these scales.

darkEnergy.title: Dark Energy
darkEnergy.description: A mysterious force responsible for the accelerating expansion of the universe, accounting for approximately 68 percent of its total contents.

exoplanets.title: Exoplanets
exoplanets.description: Worlds orbiting stars other than our Sun that might one day reveal the presence of life.

starNursery.title: Stellar Nurseries
starNursery.description: Vast clouds of gas and dust where gravity gives birth to new stars.

cosmicWeb.title: The Cosmic Web
cosmicWeb.description: The largest known structure in the universe: enormous filaments of dark matter and galaxies stretching across space, separated by vast cosmic voids.

end.question: Are you ready to begin the journey?

solar.title: Solar System
solar.intro: Our home in the vast universe. One central star and eight remarkable planets, each telling a unique story about the formation of our planetary system.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.desc: The smallest planet and the closest to the Sun. Its surface is covered with impact craters similar to those on the Moon, and it lacks a stable atmosphere that can retain heat.

venus.name: Venus
venus.desc: With a thick carbon dioxide atmosphere that creates an intense greenhouse effect, Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System.

earth.name: Earth
earth.desc: Our pale blue dot. It is the only known place in the universe with the right conditions, including liquid water and a suitable atmosphere, for life to evolve.

mars.name: Mars
mars.desc: A cold, desert world with a thin atmosphere. Mars is home to the largest volcano and some of the deepest valleys discovered in the Solar System.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.desc: The king of the planets. Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined and is home to enormous, long-lasting storms.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.desc: The jewel of the Solar System, famous for its extensive and brilliant rings made of billions of fragments of ice and rock.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.desc: The only planet whose rotational axis is tilted so dramatically that it essentially orbits the Sun on its side. It has an extremely cold atmosphere.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.desc: The farthest planet from the Sun. It is a dark, cold world with supersonic winds reaching speeds of up to 2,000 kilometers per hour.

deep.title: Deep Space
deep.intro: Beyond the Solar System, in absolute darkness and interstellar cold, extraordinary phenomena challenge our understanding of the laws of physics.

black-holes.title: Black Holes
black-holes.subtitle: Gravitational Giants and the Event Horizon
black-holes.desc: Black holes are regions of spacetime where gravity is so powerful that nothing, not even light, can escape. This remarkable image shows the first captured image of the event horizon of the supermassive black hole at the center of galaxy M87, observed by the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT).

nebulae.title: Nebulae
nebulae.subtitle: Stellar Nurseries and Cosmic Birth
nebulae.desc: Nebulae are enormous clouds of dust, hydrogen, and helium gas. This remarkable image of the Cosmic Cliffs in the Carina Nebula, captured by the James Webb Space Telescope, reveals magnificent regions where new generations of stars are born.

pulsars.title: Pulsars
pulsars.subtitle: The Rotating Lighthouses of the Universe
pulsars.desc: Pulsars are extremely dense neutron stars that rotate at extraordinary speeds. They emit powerful streams of energetic particles and electromagnetic radiation from their magnetic poles with remarkable precision, much like atomic clocks.

stats.label: Rotation Speed
stats.value: Up to hundreds of rotations per second

stats.label: Matter Density
stats.value: Billions of tons per cubic centimeter

stats.label: Magnetic Field
stats.value: Trillions of times Earth's magnetic field
